audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] says 'World Ender's stat swing and revive cancel whatever lead he built'. World Ender grants no revive. Aatrox has not had a revive on his ultimate for many patches — the champion in this matchup who revives is ZAAHEN, through Cultivation of War.
audit.why: Riot's text: World Ender — 'Aatrox unleashes his demonic form, fearing nearby enemy minions and gaining attack damage, increased healing, and Move Speed. If he gets a takedown, this effect is extended.' No revive. Cultivation of War — 'When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive.' Telling an Aatrox player they have a revive window at 6 will get them killed taking a fight they cannot survive, and it hides the fact that their OPPONENT is the one who comes back. The Teemo mirror flagged the identical false claim in that matchup's file, so this error is systemic.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now says World Ender grants no revive and points the revive at Zaahen's passive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dreaded Return is described only as a 'W pull' that 're-engages'. Riot's text has it stab in a direction and then pull enemies toward him — and the kit flags it as a knockup, so it is displacement, not just a gap-close. Nothing anywhere states that The Darkin Glaive is recastable, which is where his knockup comes from.
audit.why: Riot's text: The Darkin Glaive — 'Zaahen slashes twice on his next attack, dealing bonus damage and healing himself. Zaahen can recast this ability to have his next attack deal bonus damage and knock up his target.' So his knockup is not a separate button you can track; it is the second half of an ability he has already spent, meaning the tell is the recast, not the cast. Dreaded Return is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 and Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, which is why the entry's advice to trade in the ten seconds after his dash is right.
audit.corrected: The Darkin Glaive's recast knockup stated in wants.foe[0]; Dreaded Return's pull already carries its 14s cooldown in spikes[2].
